s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic eye symptoms with progressive vision loss and conjunctival abnormalities
key_facts: Initial visual acuity was 20/20 OD and 20/30 OS
Vision deteriorated to 20/30 OD and counting fingers OS over time
Slit lamp examination revealed subconjunctival fibrosis
Slit lamp examination revealed symblepharon formation
Slit lamp examination revealed corneal neovascularizations
Slit lamp examination revealed conjunctival hyperemia
Conjunctival biopsy and immunofluorescent histology revealed an unspecific result
Reduction in conjunctival hyperemia and corneal vascularizations after therapy

shortlist.label: Mucous Membrane Pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic eye symptoms with subconjunctival fibrosis and symblepharon formation

shortlist.label: Ocular Cicatricial Pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive vision loss and conjunctival hyperemia

shortlist.label: Linear IgA Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic eye symptoms with conjunctival abnormalities

raw.rationale: Presence of subconjunctival fibrosis, symblepharon formation, and corneal neovascularizations are more specific to Ocular Cicatricial Pemphigoid, a subtype of Mucous Membrane Pemphigoid

rejected.label: Mucous Membrane Pemphigoid
rejected.why: Too broad, as the specific ocular findings point towards a more specific subtype

rejected.label: Chronic Graft-Versus-Host Disease
rejected.why: Lack of mention of graft or transplant history

rejected.label: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome
rejected.why: Typically presents with more acute and widespread skin and mucous membrane involvement

rejected.label: Linear IgA Disease
rejected.why: Usually presents with a distinct immunofluorescence pattern, which was not found in the biopsy
